speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are a neonate presenting with seizures and lethargy three days after birth; please know I will ask you questions to find the cause. First, were your parents of advanced maternal age, or did you have any known genetic conditions in your family?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy (HIE) with secondary seizures. The clinical picture of a 31-week preterm infant with low Apgar scores, a history of chorioamnionitis, and onset of seizures and lethargy three days post-birth is highly suggestive of perinatal asphyxia leading to HIE. Immediate neuroprotective cooling and further workup for sepsis are indicated.
